Unit 28: Public Policy, Taxation, Social Welfare, Inequality & Third/Mixed Conditionals

1. taxation (n)
/tækˈseɪʃn/
hệ thống thuế khóa, việc đánh thuế (progressive taxation = thuế lũy tiến: thu nhập càng cao đóng thuế càng nhiều)
Collocation: progressive taxation, corporate taxation, heavy taxation
"Progressive taxation helps redistribute wealth and fund essential public services."
2. welfare (n)
/ˈwelfeə(r)/
phúc lợi xã hội, an sinh xã hội (không đếm được)
Collocation: social welfare system, welfare state, child welfare
"A strong social welfare system provides a safety net for unemployed and disabled citizens."
3. inequality (n)
/ˌɪnɪˈkwɒləti/
sự bất bình đẳng (về thu nhập, tài sản, cơ hội giáo dục)
Collocation: income inequality, widen wealth inequality, reduce social inequality
"Widening income inequality between the ultra-rich and working families threatens social cohesion."
4. redistribute (v)
/ˌriːdɪˈstrɪbjuːt/
tái phân phối (của cải, thu nhập từ nhóm giàu sang các dịch vụ công cho toàn dân — n: redistribution)
Collocation: redistribute wealth, redistribute tax revenue
"Governments use tax revenues to redistribute wealth through free schools and public hospitals."
5. affluent (adj)
/ˈæfluənt/
giàu có, thịnh vượng, sung túc (từ C1 thay cho 'rich / wealthy' — n: affluence)
Collocation: affluent neighbourhoods, affluent households, affluent nations
"Children born in affluent neighbourhoods often have access to better educational facilities."
6. impoverished (adj)
/ɪmˈpɒvərɪʃt/
nghèo khó, bần cùng, thiếu thốn trầm trọng (từ C1 thay cho 'very poor')
Collocation: impoverished communities, impoverished rural areas
"State scholarships enable talented students from impoverished families to attend university."
7. deficit (n)
/ˈdefɪsɪt/
sự thâm hụt ngân sách (khi chi tiêu vượt quá nguồn thu — trái nghĩa: surplus — thặng dư)
Collocation: budget deficit, reduce the national deficit, trade deficit
"Overspending without raising tax revenue can lead to a massive national budget deficit."
8. surplus (n/adj)
/ˈsɜːpləs/
số dư, sự thặng dư (ngân sách, lương thực, điện năng)
Collocation: budget surplus, trade surplus, surplus food
"When the economy grows strongly, the government can use its budget surplus to build new railways."
9. evasion (n)
/ɪˈveɪʒn/
hành vi trốn tránh bất hợp pháp (đặc biệt: tax evasion — hành vi trốn thuế)
Collocation: combat tax evasion, corporate tax evasion, strict penalties for evasion
"Closing legal loopholes to stop corporate tax evasion could recover billions for public hospitals."
10. philanthropy (n)
/fɪˈlænθrəpi/
hoạt động từ thiện quy mô lớn của giới siêu giàu/doanh nghiệp (n: philanthropist — nhà từ thiện)
Collocation: corporate philanthropy, billionaire philanthropy
"While billionaire philanthropy funds medical research, it cannot replace a fair taxation system."
11. mobility (n)
/məʊˈbɪləti/
sự dịch chuyển (social mobility = sự dịch chuyển tầng lớp xã hội: cơ hội để con nhà nghèo vươn lên)
Collocation: upward social mobility, promote social mobility
"Equitable access to quality education is the most powerful engine of upward social mobility."
12. infrastructure (n)
/ˈɪnfrəstrʌktʃə(r)/
cơ sở hạ tầng công cộng (đường sá, cầu cống, lưới điện, trường trạm — không đếm được)
Collocation: public infrastructure, modernize transport infrastructure
"Investing in rural infrastructure connects remote villages to national markets."
13. legislation (n)
/ˌledʒɪsˈleɪʃn/
luật pháp, hệ thống đạo luật (ôn tập & nâng cao chính sách công)
Collocation: enact minimum-wage legislation, labour legislation
"Enacting minimum-wage legislation protects low-skilled workers from exploitation."
14. privilege (n)
/ˈprɪvəlɪdʒ/
đặc quyền, lợi thế riêng (adj: privileged — có đặc quyền, sung túc; underprivileged — thiệt thòi)
Collocation: economic privilege, underprivileged children
"Quality healthcare should be a fundamental human right rather than a privilege for the affluent."
15. equitable (adj)
/ˈekwɪtəbl/
công bằng, bình đẳng về cơ hội cho mọi tầng lớp (= fair and impartial — n: equity)
Collocation: equitable distribution of wealth, equitable access to education
"A civilized society strives to create a more equitable economy where hard work is rewarded."

⚙️ 2. Bài Giảng Ngữ Pháp 2 Tầng (Grammar Masterclass)

🟢 Tầng 1: Câu Điều Kiện Loại 3 (Third Conditional) & Điều Kiện Hỗn Hợp (Mixed Conditional)

• 1. Câu Điều Kiện Loại 3 (Giả định trái ngược với Quá khứ — Phê phán/Rút kinh nghiệm lịch sử):
  If + S + had + V3/ed, S + would / could / might + have + V3/ed
  Ví dụ: If governments had regulated housing prices earlier, wealth inequality would not have widened so dramatically.

• 2. Câu Điều Kiện Hỗn Hợp (Mixed Conditional — Nguyên nhân trong Quá khứ dẫn đến Kết quả ở Hiện tại):
  If + S + had + V3/ed (Quá khứ), S + would / could + V-nguyên mẫu (Hiện tại — có 'now / today')
  Ví dụ: If the state had invested heavily in rural infrastructure twenty years ago, those impoverished provinces would be much more prosperous today.

🔵 Tầng 2: Đảo Ngữ Câu Điều Kiện Loại 1, 2 & 3 (Conditional Inversion Without 'If' — C1-C2)

• Thay thế 'If' bằng Đảo ngữ ở đầu câu (Vũ khí ngữ pháp Band 8.0+ GRA trong Writing Task 2):
  - Loại 1 (Should + S + V-nguyên mẫu):
    Ví dụ: Should the government abolish progressive taxation, the budget deficit will skyrocket.
  - Loại 2 (Were + S + to V):
    Ví dụ: Were authorities to close tax loopholes, billions of dollars could be redistributed to public schools.
  - Loại 3 (Had + S + V3/ed):
    Ví dụ: Had Nordic countries not built strong social welfare systems, they would not have achieved such high social mobility.

🎯 20 Câu Test Từ Vựng (Vocabulary Mastery Test)

1. Under a system of progressive ________, billionaires and large corporations pay a higher percentage of their income.
2. Unemployment benefits and state pensions are key pillars of a modern social ________ system.
3. Economists warn that extreme income ________ between executives and factory workers can trigger social unrest.
4. Tax revenues allow the state to ________ wealth from luxury sectors to public hospitals and rural schools.
5. Luxury electric cars and private golf clubs are mainly affordable for ________ households.
6. International charities build clean water wells and clinics in ________ rural villages.
7. Because government expenditure exceeded tax revenue by ten billion dollars, the country faced a severe budget ________.
8. Thanks to strong export growth, the government recorded a budget ________ and invested the extra money in healthcare.
9. Using illegal offshore bank accounts to hide profits is a serious crime known as tax ________.
10. Through generous ________, the retired billionaire donated half of his fortune to build libraries and hospitals.
11. Free university tuition promotes upward social ________ by allowing working-class children to become doctors and engineers.
12. High-speed railways, bridges, and power grids are essential components of national ________.
13. Parliament enacted new ________ to guarantee paid maternity leave for all female employees.
14. Access to clean drinking water and primary education should be a universal right, not a ________ for the rich.
15. Policymakers must ensure a more ________ distribution of medical resources between big cities and rural areas.
16. [Ôn tập Unit 27] Critics fear that global fast-food and fashion chains will ________ local cultures.
17. [Ôn tập Unit 26] By 2040, space agencies will have established a permanent base on the ________ surface.
18. [Ôn tập Unit 25] Donating blood to save strangers without any financial reward is an act of pure ________.
19. [Ôn tập Unit 24] Practicing ________ meditation for fifteen minutes daily helps employees cope with stress.
20. [Ôn tập Unit 21] An ageing population places a heavy financial ________ on state pension funds.
Điểm: 0/20

⚙️ 10 Câu Test Ngữ Pháp Ứng Dụng (Grammar Mastery Test)

1. Third Conditional: If the government had regulated banking loans in 2007, the financial crisis ________.
2. Mixed Conditional (Past Cause -> Present Result): If the state had invested in rural schools twenty years ago, those provinces ________ much more prosperous today.
3. Conditional Inversion (Type 3): ________ the company paid its taxes honestly, it would not have faced a heavy fine.
4. Conditional Inversion (Type 2): ________ authorities to abolish state scholarships, thousands of impoverished students could not attend university.
5. Conditional Inversion (Type 1): ________ the economy experience a recession next year, welfare expenditure will rise.
6. Note that 'infrastructure' and 'legislation' are uncountable: Modern transport infrastructure ________ essential for rural economic mobility.
7. Note that 'the affluent / the impoverished' take plural verbs: In many nations, the affluent ________ expected to pay progressive taxes.
8. Tax revenues collected from luxury goods ________ to fund free healthcare for underprivileged families.
9. It is imperative that the government ________ legal loopholes to prevent corporate tax evasion.
10. What truly promotes upward social mobility ________ equitable access to quality public education.
Điểm: 0/10

Scholarship Officer: Good morning, National Social Mobility and Education Foundation, Officer Claire Bennett speaking. How may I assist you?
University Applicant: Hello Ms. Bennett! My name is Marcus Gallagher. I am calling to inquire about the Equitable Future Scholarship for first-generation university students.
Scholarship Officer: I would be glad to help you, Marcus! Could you spell your surname so I can create your application profile?
University Applicant: Yes, it is Gallagher. G - A - L - L - A - G - H - E - R. 💡 Đáp án câu 1 (Họ ứng viên học bổng): GALLAGHER
Scholarship Officer: Thank you. Our foundation is funded by progressive taxation and corporate philanthropy to help students from low-income families study at top universities.
University Applicant: What is the maximum annual household income allowed to qualify for the full grant?
Scholarship Officer: To qualify for the full grant, your family's annual income must be below 24,000 pounds. 💡 Đáp án câu 2 (Mức trần thu nhập hộ gia đình): 24,000 / 24000
University Applicant: My parents earn around 19,000 pounds, so we qualify. Does the scholarship only cover tuition fees, or does it help with accommodation too?
Scholarship Officer: In addition to full tuition, each scholar receives a living allowance of 6,500 pounds per year for accommodation and books. 💡 Đáp án câu 3 (Trợ cấp sinh hoạt phí mỗi năm): 6,500 / 6500
University Applicant: Six thousand five hundred pounds will lift a huge financial burden off my parents! Which degree subjects are prioritized this year?
Scholarship Officer: Last year we focused on Law, but this year priority is given to students applying for Renewable Engineering and Medicine. 💡 Bẫy năm ngoái (Law) vs ưu tiên năm nay câu 4: Renewable Engineering / Engineering
University Applicant: That is fantastic—I am applying for Civil and Renewable Engineering! What documents do I need to submit to verify my family's income?
Scholarship Officer: Please submit your high school transcript and your parents' official Tax Return certificate from the last financial year. 💡 Đáp án câu 5 (Giấy tờ xác minh thu nhập): Tax Return
University Applicant: When is the final closing date for scholarship applications?
Scholarship Officer: All applications must be submitted online by the 31st of March. Best of luck with your engineering studies, Marcus! 💡 Đáp án câu 6 (Hạn chót nộp đơn): 31st March / March 31

📰 IELTS Academic Reading: Passage & Questions

[Paragraph A - The Growing Divide Between the Affluent and the Impoverished]
Over the past three decades, technological innovation and global trade have generated immense wealth, yet the benefits have not been shared equally. In many countries, the gap between affluent elites and impoverished working families has widened to historic levels. While billionaires accumulate vast fortunes, millions of ordinary citizens struggle with stagnant wages and rising housing costs. Sociologists warn that extreme income inequality erodes social cohesion and turns quality healthcare and higher education into an exclusive privilege rather than an equitable right.

[Paragraph B - The Debate Over Progressive Taxation and Corporate Evasion]
To narrow this divide, economists advocate a fair system of progressive taxation, whereby high earners and large corporations contribute a larger share of their income to the state. Opponents argue that excessive tax rates reduce the financial incentive for entrepreneurs to innovate and invest. However, fiscal studies reveal that national budget deficits are rarely caused by high public spending alone; rather, they stem from legal loopholes that allow multinational firms to engage in tax evasion. Had governments closed these loopholes decades ago, they would have collected trillions of dollars in budget surpluses.

[Paragraph C - Investing in Social Welfare and Upward Mobility]
While private billionaire philanthropy plays a helpful role in funding charities, it cannot replace a comprehensive social welfare system enacted through national legislation. When governments redistribute tax revenue to modernize rural infrastructure, subsidize public healthcare, and provide university scholarships for underprivileged youth, they create a powerful engine of upward social mobility. Were a nation to neglect these public investments, talented children from poor backgrounds could never reach their full potential.
Điểm: 0/6
